prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale EO ground segment. Mission Control Center (MCC, Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing; coordinates with PPF on modes/downlink/gaps; sends constraints to MPS; escalation console lead→discipline lead→mission mgmt. Flight dynamics deliveries must include validity interval, frame, generation time, use statement. Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, Mistral): orbit catalog; ephemerides/events to MCC, MPS, PPF; Star Tracker Mask File; Ephemeris Delta Note; maneuver recommendations to Spacecraft Operations Team; geometry to Payload Calibration Team. Payload Processing Facility (PPF, Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Processing Clusters; if Primary misses window, scheduling service moves jobs to Backup (same container image/rules); Backup writes fallback provenance used by Product Quality Service (PQS); both down→suspend, keep raw in staging, notify MCC via operational event channel. Telemetry Ingest Service verifies station files (size, sequence, checksum, time); Pass Replay Packet. Levels L0/L1A/L1B/L2; each records build, calibration baseline, ancillary versions for audit regeneration. Payload Calibration Team owns approved calibration baseline, reviews trends; changes tested on sample scenes vs baseline; radiometric/geometric/saturation changes require spec update before release. PQS: checks solutions; uses patch bundle to update calibration checks; quality flags (missing packets, timing discontinuity, saturation, cloud uncertainty, geolocation residuals, fallback) in metadata; delivery hold on failed checks/missing ancillary/blocking review; produces Product Hold List; held products stay in staging, not delivered. Long Term Archive (Granite): stores products tagged operational/test/reprocessed; sends Storage Watermark Snapshot daily. Network Control System (Lantern): WAN, allocations, contacts; antenna/link/timing/routing to MCC; uses Security Exception Ticket to restrict paths; shall keep last validated routing, reject unreviewed changes during transfers. Mission Planning System (MPS, Cedar): requests from User Services Portal/MCC; command preparation package to MCC. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): validates commands; rejects unapproved/unprovenanced/expired/out-of-window. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report, Laser Retroreflector Window. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate)→MCC; Kiruna, Svalbard X-Band→PPF.

New part:
S176: Recovery after suspension prioritizes products with contractual latency commitments, then processes remaining scenes in acquisition order unless mission management approves a different backlog rule.
S177: Long Term Archive is the authoritative repository for Sentinel Vale raw downlink, auxiliary data, processing inputs, generated products, and operational metadata after routine production has completed.
S178: Archive admission begins only after Payload Processing Facility has delivered the product package, associated quality metadata, and checksum evidence required by the configured acceptance rule.
S179: Each accepted object is assigned a persistent identifier that remains stable across media migration, catalogue refresh, and later reprocessing campaigns.
S180: The repository stores object content separately from searchable metadata so that catalogue publication can proceed without exposing internal storage paths.
S181: Catalogue records are published to User Services Portal after Product Quality Service has set the public quality status and the embargo rule has been evaluated.
S182: Products under operational review remain discoverable only to authorized mission staff until the release condition is cleared.
S183: User Services Portal provides search, preview, order, and download functions through a browser interface and documented machine interfaces.
S184: Download services support resumable transfer, integrity verification, and rate controls that protect mission operations from excessive external demand.
S185: Registered users receive authorization scopes based on mission policy, contractual access rights, and applicable data licensing constraints.
S186: Anonymous access is allowed only for product classes that have been approved for open dissemination by mission management.
S187: Long Term Archive retains raw acquisition data for the life of the mission and for the post-mission preservation period defined in the archive policy.
S188: Standard Level 1 and Level 2 products are retained online while demand, contractual latency, or reprocessing dependence justifies low-latency access.
S189: Older product copies may be moved to lower-cost storage when catalogue metadata, checksums, and restore procedures remain available.
S190: Deletion is performed only against superseded temporary products, expired working copies, or objects covered by an approved disposal rule.
S191: Retention exceptions require traceability to the approving authority, the affected product classes, and the expected operational impact.
S192: Reprocessing is triggered when calibration improvements, processor corrections, orbit updates, or quality investigations materially change product fitness for use.
S193: Payload Calibration Team may request a reprocessing campaign when validation evidence shows a systematic radiometric or geometric issue.
S194: Mistral publishes orbit quality state changes to the archive operations queue before catalogue validity flags are updated.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
